recognize_zh: 骨髓切片 CD34 免疫染色幾乎全為藍色背景，只有零星單顆細胞與小血管內皮呈棕色陽性；提醒 ML-DS 的巨核母細胞常為 CD34 陰性，不能以 CD34 低估芽細胞比例。
features: Cellular marrow with a mixed population of hematopoietic cells, predominantly CD34-negative
Only rare scattered single CD34-positive cells with membranous/cytoplasmic brown staining
Positive staining of small capillary endothelial cells serves as internal control
No clusters or sheets of CD34-positive blasts
describe_en: CD34 immunohistochemical stain of the bone marrow core biopsy shows a cellular marrow in which the vast majority of hematopoietic cells are negative. Only rare scattered CD34-positive cells are present, with no clusters or sheets, and small vessels stain positively as an internal control. Because megakaryoblasts in myeloid leukemia associated with Down syndrome are frequently CD34-negative, this pattern does not exclude an increase in blasts; correlation with aspirate morphology, flow cytometry, and megakaryocytic markers (CD61/CD42b) is required.

ddx.vs: Both show rare CD34-positive cells, so separation relies on aspirate blast count, atypical megakaryocytes, and megakaryocytic marker staining rather than CD34.
Those typically show clusters or sheets of CD34-positive blasts, unlike the rare scattered positivity here.
CD34 may highlight increased vascularity and blasts in fibrotic marrow; reticulin stain and H&E architecture are needed to separate it.
